properties.formal: forall s, length (normalise_code s) <= length s
properties.description: normalising code only ever removes characters
assumptions: text modelled as List Char
splitlines modelled as splitting on '\n'

properties.formal: framed ['X\na', 'b', 'c'] <> framed ['X', 'a\nb', 'c']
properties.description: a field cannot imitate the boundary between two others — the newline-joined payload could, and two distinct properties shared a cache key
assumptions: text modelled as List Char
stated on the witness that collided under the old joining

properties.formal: normalise_formal 'a in b' = normalise_formal 'a∈b' /\ normalise_formal 'ainb' <> normalise_formal 'a∈b'
properties.description: the membership word is an operator only on a word boundary — 'ainb' is an identifier, and merging it with 'a∈b' put two properties under one key
assumptions: text modelled as List Char
stated on the witness that collided before word boundaries were respected

properties.formal: forall ws, is_space ws '\u001c' /\ is_space ws '\u001f' /\ is_space ws '\u001b' = ws '\u001b' /\ is_space ws '\u0020' = ws '\u0020'
properties.description: the extension covers U+001C and U+001F and stops there — U+001B and U+0020 are left to Unicode
assumptions: char::is_whitespace left abstract as ws, so the claim holds whatever Unicode says
the inclusive range '\u{1c}'..='\u{1f}' modelled as a comparison on code points

properties.formal: forall ws, ws '\u001c' = false -> is_space ws '\u001c' <> ws '\u001c'
properties.description: is_space is not char::is_whitespace — on U+001C the two disagree, which is why swapping one for the other moves every cache key
assumptions: char::is_whitespace left abstract as ws
that U+001C is not Unicode White_Space enters as a hypothesis, not as a fact of the model

properties.formal: forall p s, exists z, s = rstrip p s ++ z /\ (forall c in z, p c)
properties.description: rstrip cuts a suffix and nothing else, and every character it cuts is space
assumptions: text modelled as List Char
quantified over the trimming predicate, so it covers pystr::is_space in particular
trim_matches modelled as dropping a maximal run of matching characters from an end

properties.formal: forall p s t c, rstrip p s = t ++ [c] -> not (p c)
properties.description: whatever rstrip returns, its last character is not space — the run it removes is maximal
assumptions: text modelled as List Char
quantified over the trimming predicate, so it covers pystr::is_space in particular
trim_matches modelled as dropping a maximal run of matching characters from an end

properties.formal: forall p s, rstrip p (rstrip p s) = rstrip p s
properties.description: rstripping a line twice is rstripping it once, so normalisation is a fixed point
assumptions: text modelled as List Char
quantified over the trimming predicate, so it covers pystr::is_space in particular
trim_matches modelled as dropping a maximal run of matching characters from an end

properties.formal: forall p s, exists pre suf, s = pre ++ strip p s ++ suf /\ (forall c in pre, p c) /\ (forall c in suf, p c)
properties.description: strip cuts one run from each end and nothing from the middle, and every character it cuts is space
assumptions: text modelled as List Char
quantified over the trimming predicate, so it covers pystr::is_space in particular
trim_matches modelled as dropping a maximal run of matching characters from an end

properties.formal: forall p s, (forall c t, strip p s = c :: t -> not (p c)) /\ (forall t c, strip p s = t ++ [c] -> not (p c))
properties.description: neither end of a stripped string is space — both runs removed are maximal
assumptions: text modelled as List Char
quantified over the trimming predicate, so it covers pystr::is_space in particular
trim_matches modelled as dropping a maximal run of matching characters from an end
an empty result satisfies both halves vacuously

properties.formal: forall p s, strip p (strip p s) = strip p s
properties.description: stripping twice is stripping once, which is what makes the cache key stable under re-normalisation
assumptions: text modelled as List Char
quantified over the trimming predicate, so it covers pystr::is_space in particular
trim_matches modelled as dropping a maximal run of matching characters from an end

properties.formal: forall a br b, (forall c in a, not (is_break c)) -> is_break br -> br <> '\r' -> splitlines (a ++ br :: b) = a :: splitlines b
properties.description: a boundary closes the text before it as one whole line and is itself dropped; with b empty this is why a trailing newline makes no empty last line
assumptions: text modelled as List Char, a line as the characters between two boundaries
the boundary set is the ten characters the Rust match names
carriage return excluded here and covered by the bare-CR property

properties.formal: forall a b, (forall c in a, not (is_break c)) -> splitlines (a ++ '\r' :: '\n' :: b) = a :: splitlines b
properties.description: CR LF is a single boundary — the line feed is consumed with the carriage return and starts no empty line
assumptions: text modelled as List Char, a line as the characters between two boundaries
the boundary set is the ten characters the Rust match names

properties.formal: forall a b, (forall c in a, not (is_break c)) -> (forall t, b <> '\n' :: t) -> splitlines (a ++ '\r' :: b) = a :: splitlines b
properties.description: a carriage return not followed by a line feed is a boundary on its own, including at the end of the text
assumptions: text modelled as List Char, a line as the characters between two boundaries
the boundary set is the ten characters the Rust match names

properties.formal: forall s l c, l in splitlines s -> c in l -> not (is_break c)
properties.description: no line handed back still contains a boundary — the split is complete, so a vertical tab cannot hide inside a line
assumptions: text modelled as List Char, a line as the characters between two boundaries
the boundary set is the ten characters the Rust match names

properties.formal: forall s, (forall c in s, not (is_break c)) -> splitlines s = (if s = [] then [] else [s])
properties.description: text with no boundary is one line, and empty text is no lines at all — Python's '' splits to nothing, not to one empty line
assumptions: text modelled as List Char, a line as the characters between two boundaries
the boundary set is the ten characters the Rust match names

properties.formal: forall ls, length (imports ls) + length (body ls) = length ls
properties.description: every line is either hoisted as an import or kept in the body — none is dropped and none is duplicated
assumptions: the import test is left abstract, so the claim holds whatever counts as an import

properties.formal: forall ls, length (body ls) = length (source_lines ls)
properties.description: every surviving line records where it came from — the two lists a batch entry is rebased through cannot drift apart
assumptions: the import test is left abstract, so the claim holds whatever counts as an import

properties.formal: forall ls n num, num in source_lines ls n -> n <= num < n + length ls
properties.description: a recorded line number names a line that exists — it never points before the file or past its end
assumptions: numbering starts at n, so the Rust's 1-based call is n = 1

properties.formal: forall ls n num line, (num, line) in zip (source_lines ls n) (body ls n) -> ls[num - n] = line
properties.description: the number recorded beside a body line is the line that produced it — the whole basis for attributing a batch error to the right proof
assumptions: numbering starts at n, so the Rust's 1-based call is n = 1
the import test is left abstract, so the claim holds whatever counts as an import

properties.formal: forall before body, 0 < body -> last_line - first_line + 1 = body
properties.description: the lines an entry claims in the batch are exactly the lines of its body, so no error inside the span belongs to a neighbour
assumptions: line numbers are 1-based, as Lean reports them
one entry's emission modelled as before ++ namespace :: body ++ [end], which is what build_batch pushes

properties.formal: forall before line, not (covers first_line (last_line before 0) line)
properties.description: an entry whose body is empty claims no line at all — last_line sits below first_line rather than swallowing the namespace line
assumptions: line numbers are 1-based, as Lean reports them

properties.formal: forall before ns body end j, j < length body -> batch[first_line + j - 1] = body[j]
properties.description: the batch line an entry's span points at holds that entry's own body line — the other half of attributing an error correctly
assumptions: one entry's emission modelled as before ++ namespace :: body ++ [end], which is what build_batch pushes

properties.formal: forall before body line, covers first_line last_line line -> line - first_line < body
properties.description: an error the batch attributes to an entry always indexes a recorded line — rebase never falls through to reporting the batch position as if it were the caller's
assumptions: line numbers are 1-based, as Lean reports them
body is the length of the entry's source_lines, which split_imports keeps equal to its body

properties.formal: forall ms code, (exists m in ms, severity m = warning and has_sorry (data m)) -> success code (collect ms) = false
properties.description: a proof with a hole in it never passes — the sorry Lean reports as a warning is promoted into the errors, and a non-empty error list is not a success
assumptions: the two substring tests are left abstract, so the claim holds whatever they are spelled with

properties.formal: forall m in promoted ms, severity m = error
properties.description: a sorry that Lean called a warning is reported as an error, not passed through with its original severity
assumptions: the substring test for sorry is left abstract

properties.formal: forall ms, real_errors ms <> [] -> head (collect ms) = head (real_errors ms)
properties.description: promoted sorries are appended after the real errors, so the first thing Lean said stays the first thing reported
assumptions: the two substring tests are left abstract

properties.formal: forall code errors, code <> some 0 -> success code errors = false
properties.description: an exit code other than zero is never a pass, however empty the diagnostics are
assumptions: the exit code modelled as Option Nat, absent when the process was killed

properties.formal: forall rules, (forall r in rules, not (claims r)) -> lookup rules = fallback
properties.description: a diagnostic no rule claims gets the fallback advice rather than nothing
assumptions: whether a rule claims a diagnostic and whether it answers are left abstract

properties.formal: forall r rest hint, claims r and answer r = some hint -> lookup (r :: rest) = hint
properties.description: order is the semantics: the earliest rule that both claims the diagnostic and produces advice is the one that answers
assumptions: whether a rule claims a diagnostic and whether it answers are left abstract

properties.formal: forall r rest, claims r and answer r = none -> lookup (r :: rest) = lookup rest
properties.description: a rule that claims a diagnostic but produces nothing does not swallow it — the walk continues to the rules below rather than falling to the fallback
assumptions: whether a rule claims a diagnostic and whether it answers are left abstract

properties.formal: describes (with_trailing_space) (recorded) = true
properties.description: trailing whitespace in the source does not make a property stale — normalise_code rstrips every line before the comparison
assumptions: text modelled as List Char, one list per line where lines matter
splitlines modelled as splitting on '\n', which is all the witness contains
stated on a witness rather than universally, as the collision properties are

properties.formal: describes (reindented) (recorded) = false
properties.description: reindenting a function DOES make its property stale — normalise_code preserves leading whitespace because indentation is meaning, so a function moved one level deeper no longer matches what was recorded
assumptions: text modelled as List Char, one list per line where lines matter
splitlines modelled as splitting on '\n', which is all the witness contains
stated on the witness that the README claimed would still match

properties.formal: forall ms k s, s in spans ms k -> k + 2 <= first s
properties.description: no entry claims a line before the place it was laid out at
assumptions: an entry is modelled by its body length, the batch by the lengths in order
the next entry's offset is this one's plus its body plus three, which is the namespace, end and blank lines build_batch pushes
line numbers are 1-based, as Lean reports them

properties.formal: forall ms k m line s, s in spans ms (k + m + 3) -> covers (this entry) line -> not (covers s line)
properties.description: no batch line falls inside two entries, so an error is never reported against a proof that did not produce it — verify_batch hands each error to whichever entry covers it
assumptions: an entry is modelled by its body length, the batch by the lengths in order
the next entry's offset is this one's plus its body plus three, which is the namespace, end and blank lines build_batch pushes
line numbers are 1-based, as Lean reports them
